All of these campaigns are still showing Eligible (Limited), so they aren't blocked; Google is warning that they'll reach fewer people. Your microsoft-365 campaign has 0 impressions and ₹0 spent since 29 Sep, so that one needs fixing first.

Fix 1: "Missing enough relevant keywords" (7 campaigns)

Google shows this when an ad group has too few keywords, or when the keywords don't match the ad text and landing page closely enough. Do this in each campaign:

  1. Add more keywords. Aim for 15–25 keywords per ad group. Open the campaign, go to Recommendations, and apply the "Add new keywords" suggestions. You can also use Tools → Keyword Planner and enter the product name plus your landing page URL.
  2. Use phrase and broad match together. Exact-only or very narrow keywords often get flagged for low search volume. Your bidding should be Maximize Conversions or Target CPA, because broad match only works well with automated bidding.
  3. Put each ad group's keywords in its ads. Your headlines should repeat the main keywords. For example, if the keyword is "crowdstrike falcon price", a headline should include "CrowdStrike Falcon".
  4. Split the campaign into themed ad groups. If a campaign only has "Ad group 1", create groups such as Product name, Pricing/Quote, Managed service and Alternatives. Give each group its own keywords and ads.
  5. Check the landing page. It should name the product (Trend Micro EDR, Sophos, Wazuh, etc.) in its title and opening text.
  6. Pause keywords marked "Low search volume", and replace them with more common terms.

Example additions for TrendmicroEDR: "trend micro edr", "trend vision one", "trend micro xdr", "trend micro endpoint security", "trend micro apex one", "edr solution", "endpoint detection and response", "managed edr services", "edr pricing", "ransomware protection for business".

Fix 2: "All ads limited by policy" (microsoft-365)

This is almost certainly because of the trademark policy. "Microsoft 365", "Office", "Excel" and "OneDrive" are Microsoft trademarks, and Google limits ads that use them in the text. To check, go to Ads, hover over the status, and the policy name will show.

To fix it, choose one of these:

  • Option A (best if you're a Microsoft partner): Ask Microsoft to authorize your Google Ads account through Google's trademark authorization form. Your Microsoft partner contact or Partner Center support can submit it with your Google Ads customer ID. After approval, the ads change to Eligible.
  • Option B (quick fix): Remove "Microsoft", "365", "Office", "Excel" and "OneDrive" from your headlines, descriptions and display paths. Use wording like "Business Email & Productivity Suite" or "Cloud Productivity for Teams". You can still keep the trademarks as keywords, because keywords aren't limited.

Also replace the weak keywords. "microsoft 365 excel", "apps", "onedrive", "office" and "online" bring in consumers and people looking for support, not buyers. Use these instead: "microsoft 365 business premium", "microsoft 365 partner india", "microsoft 365 licensing for business", "buy microsoft 365 for company", "microsoft 365 migration services", "microsoft 365 csp partner".

If impressions stay at 0 after these fixes

Check these account-level items:

  • Billing: under Billing → Summary, make sure there's no payment problem.
  • Advertiser verification: complete it if Google has asked you to.
  • Bidding: on a new account with no conversions, use Maximize Clicks with a max CPC limit, or Maximize Conversions. Don't use a Target CPA that's set too low.
  • Location: set it to "Presence" targeting, and confirm the right cities or country are selected.
  • Ad strength: each responsive search ad should be at least "Good", with 10–15 headlines and 4 descriptions.

Some campaigns may stay Eligible (Limited) even after these fixes. For example, Google limits ads that use other brands' trademarks (Microsoft, CrowdStrike, Sophos) unless the brand owner has authorized you, and some keywords have low search volume. A campaign can still get impressions and leads while it shows "Limited".

If you send me the current keywords and ad text for each campaign, I can write a replacement keyword list and ads for all eight.

Copilot said:
Press Enter to navigate links and actions

The screenshot shows the actual reason, and it isn't the trademark issue I suspected earlier. Google has flagged the ad under "Misleading Representation". That means Google thinks the ad or the landing page may make users believe something about who you are, for example that you are Microsoft or officially linked to Microsoft, without enough proof.

Waiting won't change this status. It stays Eligible (Limited) until you fix what triggered it and ask for a re-review.

What usually triggers it, and what to fix

1. The ad text implies a link to Microsoft

  • Remove or reword claims such as "Partner", "Certified", "Official" and "Authorized". That includes "Licensing Partner in India" from the headlines I gave you. Only keep them if your landing page proves them, for example with a Microsoft Partner badge and your Partner ID.
  • Make sure no headline reads as if the ad comes from Microsoft. Your business name in the ad should be ISS Technologies. Check this under Assets → Business name.

2. The ad mentions "support" for Microsoft products

  • Google is strict about third-party technical support for software brands. Remove "24x7 Support" and "Expert Setup & 24x7 Support" from the ad.
  • Pause the keyword "microsoft 365 support services".

3. The landing page doesn't show clearly who you are

This is the most common cause. The page the ad links to should show:

  • ISS Technologies as the company name, with your logo
  • your full business address, phone number and work email
  • an About Us section and a Privacy Policy link
  • clear wording that you're a reseller or service provider, for example: "ISS Technologies is a Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider. Microsoft 365 is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation."
  • no Microsoft logo used as if it were your own branding, and no "Buy" or pricing claims you can't back up

4. Your advertiser account isn't verified

  • Go to Admin → Advertiser verification and complete it if it's pending. Unverified accounts are more likely to be flagged under this policy.

Then request a re-review

  1. Make the changes above, starting with the ad text and the landing page.
  2. Go back to this status, then click Appeal → "Fixed the violation" and submit.
  3. Google usually responds within 1–2 business days. If you submit today, expect an answer by around Friday, 30 Oct – Monday, 2 Nov.

If you only click Appeal without changing anything, Google will usually keep the limitation.

Replacement headlines without partner or support claims

Use these in place of "Licensing Partner in India" and "Expert Setup & 24x7 Support":

  • Business Email for Companies
  • Cloud Email Migration Help
  • Request a Licensing Quote

Send me your landing page link and I can check what on it might be triggering the policy.

The policy detail and your ad editor screenshots point to the likely cause. The ad's final URL is https://updated-m365-a3om.vercel.app/. That's a temporary hosting address, not the ISS Technologies website. Google's policy, shown in your screenshot, says you can't hide information about "your identity, affiliations, or qualifications." An ad about Microsoft 365 that links to an unbranded vercel.app address can look as if it's posing as Microsoft. Adding keywords won't change this.

I tried to open that page to check its content, but nothing was returned, so I couldn't review what's on it.

What to change, in order of importance

1. Move the landing page to your company domain (most important)

  • Host the page on your own website, for example https://www.isstechnologies.in/microsoft-365 (use your real domain).
  • Or, if you want to keep the page on Vercel, connect a custom domain such as m365.isstechnologies.in (Vercel → Project → Settings → Domains), then use that address as the ad's Final URL.
  • The domain in the ad must match your business name. Google treats a temporary or unbranded domain as a strong warning sign.

2. Change the ad description

Your current description is: "Licensing, setup, security and ongoing support for your Microsoft 365 environment."

Its wording sounds like official Microsoft support. Replace it with something like:

  • "ISS Technologies helps businesses with cloud email licensing, migration and security."

3. Change the display path

  • Change services to services or email.

4. Make the landing page show clearly who you are

The page should show:

  • the ISS Technologies name and logo at the top, not a Microsoft logo
  • your company address, phone number and email, plus About Us and Privacy Policy links
  • a disclaimer near the bottom: "ISS Technologies is an independent IT services provider and Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider. Microsoft 365 is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation." Only mention Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider if you hold that status.
  • no "Official", "Authorized" or "Certified Partner" claims unless the page also shows proof, such as your Microsoft Partner ID or badge

5. Check the business name and account details

  • Assets → Business name: set it to ISS Technologies.
  • Admin → Advertiser verification: complete it if it's pending. Use the same company name as on the landing page.

Then save the ad

According to the panel in your screenshot, once you edit the ad and save the changes, Google automatically reviews it again. You don't need to appeal separately. If you save without making changes, the ad stays limited. The review usually takes 1–2 business days.

The Vercel address is most likely the main cause. Your other campaigns may also link to vercel.app pages. If they do, move them to your company domain too, or they could get the same policy flag.

  2. Go to Settings → Domains.
  3. Type m365.isstechnologies.in and click Add.
  4. Vercel will show "Invalid Configuration" and a DNS record to create. It's usually:
TypeName / HostValue / Points to
CNAMEm365cname.vercel-dns.com

Vercel sometimes gives a project-specific value instead of cname.vercel-dns.com, so copy exactly what it shows.

Step 2: Add the DNS record where your domain is managed

Whoever manages isstechnologies.in (for example GoDaddy, Cloudflare, BigRock, Hostinger, Route 53 or Azure DNS) needs to:

  1. Open the DNS settings for isstechnologies.in.
  2. Add a record with:
    • Type: CNAME
    • Name/Host: m365
    • Value/Target: the value Vercel showed
    • TTL: default, or 1 hour
  3. Save.

If you use Cloudflare, set the record to "DNS only" (grey cloud) so Vercel can issue the SSL certificate.

Don't change any existing records, especially the website (@, www) or email (MX) records. You're only adding one new record.

If you don't manage the domain yourself, send your IT or web team the table above and ask them to add it.

Step 3: Check it's working

  • Go back to Vercel → Settings → Domains. Within a few minutes to an hour, the status should change to "Valid Configuration" with a green tick, and Vercel sets up HTTPS automatically.
  • Open in your browser and confirm your page loads.
  • In Vercel, you can set the new domain as Primary and redirect the old address to it.

Step 4: Update the Google Ads ad

  1. Go to Campaigns → microsoft-365 → Ads, then edit the ad.
  2. Change Final URL to https://m365.isstechnologies.in/.
  3. Change the display path to services.
  4. Update the description as I suggested earlier, to remove the "support for your Microsoft 365 environment" wording.
  5. Save. Google will automatically review the ad again, usually within 1–2 business days.

If you want microsoft-365 instead

That address means your main website (wherever isstechnologies.in is hosted) has to send that page to Vercel, or you rebuild the page on the main site. Your web team would need to do that, so the subdomain is much quicker, and Google accepts it because it's still your company domain.

Your other campaigns (AWS, Forcepoint, VAPT, Wazuh, Sophos, CrowdStrike, Trend Micro EDR) may also use vercel.app links. If they do, do the same for each one, for example aws.isstechnologies.in and edr.isstechnologies.in, then update their Final URLs.

FieldValue
TypeCNAME
Namem365
Points to / Targetcname.vercel-dns.com (or the value Vercel showed)

  1. Click Add Record.

If Hostinger already has a record named m365, delete it first. This only works if the domain uses Hostinger's nameservers, which is the default for domains bought there. If you've moved the nameservers elsewhere, such as Cloudflare, add the record there instead.

The policy that flagged your ad also covers using a business name that "does not clearly represent the advertised business." If your ad and Google Ads account say ISS Technologies but the website is cyberxpertz.online, Google may flag it again for the same reason.

To avoid that, make the names consistent:

  • Your advertiser verification details should name the same company the website names.
  • Keep the Microsoft disclaimer on the page: "Microsoft 365 is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation. CyberXpertz is an independent IT services provider."

m365.isstechnologies.in is still the safer choice if you can get access to that domain's DNS, because it matches your company name directly. If you can't, m365.cyberxpertz.online will work, as long as the branding is consistent everywhere.

That's normal at this stage. The campaign status only updates after Google finishes reviewing the edited ad, which usually takes 1–2 business days. It doesn't change straight after you save, and it won't change at all if the ad itself hasn't been edited.

Check where you are

1. Is the new domain working?

  • In Vercel → Settings → Domains, does m365.cyberxpertz.online show Valid Configuration with a blue tick?
  • Does open your page in a browser?
  • If not, finish the Hostinger DNS step first. Google can't approve an ad whose link doesn't load.

2. Have you edited the ad itself? Go to Campaigns → microsoft-365 → Ads → hover over the ad → Edit and confirm:

  • Final URL is https://m365.cyberxpertz.online/, not the vercel.app address
  • Display path is services, not services
  • The description no longer says "ongoing support for your Microsoft 365 environment"
  • The headlines don't include Partner, Certified, Official or 24/7 Support
  • You clicked Save

3. What does the ad status say now? Go to the Ads tab, not the Campaigns page, and check the ad's status:

Ad statusWhat it meansWhat to do
Under reviewGoogle is checking your changesWait 1–2 business days. Don't edit it again.
Eligible (Limited) – Misleading Representation with an old dateYour changes weren't saved, or nothing changedMake the edits above and save again
EligibleThe ad is fixedThe campaign status will update within a few hours

Expected timeline

If you saved the edited ad today (Thursday, 29 Oct), the review should finish by Friday, 30 Oct, or Monday, 2 Nov at the latest. The campaign status should then change to Eligible.

If it's still limited after the review

  1. Hover over the status and click Appeal → "Fixed the violation".
  2. If that's rejected, contact Google Ads support (Help → Contact us). Ask which specific element (the ad text, the landing page or the business name) is triggering Misleading Representation.

Send me a screenshot of the Ads tab showing the ad's status, and I'll tell you which of these situations you're in.

The intro paragraph says: "Buy, migrate and manage Microsoft 365 with a Microsoft Solutions Partner."

  • If ISS has this designation: add proof. Show the official Microsoft Solutions Partner badge and your Partner ID on the page, for example in the footer or an "About us" section.
  • If it doesn't: change the line to "Buy, migrate and manage Microsoft 365 with ISS Technologies, an independent IT services provider."

Google treats an unverifiable affiliation claim as misleading.

The page shows the ISS Technologies logo, but the domain is cyberxpertz.online. Add a line in the header or footer that links the two, for example: "CyberXpertz is a digital services brand of ISS Technologies."

  • Bullet: "24/7 M365ProCare – ISS Technologies' own managed service team after go-live."

  • ISS Technologies, with your full registered address
  • Phone: +91 98483 03850, plus a business email address
  • links to Privacy Policy, Terms and Contact / About Us
  • disclaimer: "Microsoft and Microsoft 365 are trademarks of Microsoft Corporation. ISS Technologies is an independent provider and is not Microsoft."

5. The brochure PDF

Check that it doesn't contain the same partner claim without proof.

  5. Remove Partner, Certified, Official and Support wording from the headlines and descriptions, then Save.

The ad will show Under review. Expect a result in about 1–2 business days, so by Friday, 30 Oct, or Monday, 2 Nov at the latest.
